condition: Components of the BCLC staging model
recommendation: The BCLC staging model is based on tumor burden, liver function, and performance status (PS), and the 2022 version further incorporates AFP, ALBI score, Child-Pugh, and MELD score for refined assessment.
hint: Although these new parameters are included, they may not alter the prognosis if liver function does not meet the criteria for optimal treatment.
original_text: Based on tumor burden, liver function and physical status Refined by AFP, ALBI score, Child-Pugh, MELD

recommendation: For liver function assessment, in addition to Child-Pugh and MELD scores, the ALBI score (albumin-bilirubin) is recommended to stratify compensated liver function with additional granularity.
hint: Child-Pugh was already abandoned as the sole criterion in the previous version and needs to be combined with more indicators.
original_text: compensated liver function could be stratified with additional granularity by using the albumin-bilirubin (ALBI) score

condition: Role of AFP in prognosis assessment
recommendation: AFP concentration should be included in the BCLC model as a prognostic parameter, irrespective of tumor burden.
hint: High AFP is generally associated with poorer prognosis and higher recurrence risk.
original_text: while also adding alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) concentration, irrespective of tumour burden.

condition: Definition of Clinically Significant Portal Hypertension (CSPH)
recommendation: Clinically Significant Portal Hypertension (CSPH) is defined by a hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) >10 mmHg, or clinical signs such as prior variceal bleeding.
hint: Prior variceal bleeding reflects more advanced liver disease but does not necessarily warrant specific exclusion from treatment; comprehensive assessment is needed.
original_text: Prior variceal bleeding also reflects more advanced liver disease with clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH)... defined by a hepatic venous pressure gradient [HVPG] >10 mmHg

recommendation: Performance Status (PS) assessment should incorporate tumor-related symptoms but must exclude baseline symptoms already present prior to cancer diagnosis (e.g., due to comorbidities).
hint: Differentiating symptoms caused by tumor vs. liver function/comorbidities is crucial for staging (BCLC C vs BCLC D).
original_text: Regarding performance status (PS) assessment... it is important to highlight that PS assessment should incorporate tumour-related symptoms but not baseline symptoms already present prior to cancer diagnosis

recommendation: Very early stage (BCLC 0) is defined as a solitary HCC ≤2 cm without vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread in a patient with preserved liver function and no cancer-related symptoms.
hint: Patients with severe liver dysfunction but eligible for transplant are also classified here; otherwise, they are BCLC D.
original_text: Very early stage (BCLC 0) This is defined as a solitary HCC ≤2 cm without vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread in a patient with preserved liver function and no cancer-related symptoms.

recommendation: For BCLC 0 patients who are potential transplant candidates and eligible for surgery, resection is the first choice, although Liver Transplantation (LT) should be considered due to high recurrence risk.
hint: Pathological features (e.g., microvascular invasion) may prompt consideration for transplant.
original_text: Therefore, if transplantation is an option and patients fulfil the criteria for surgery, resection should be the first choice.

condition: Preferred treatment for BCLC 0 (Not transplant candidates)
recommendation: For BCLC 0 patients where LT is not feasible, ablation is the first treatment approach, offering survival outcomes similar to resection.
hint: Ablation is typically the alternative to resection, especially when LT is not feasible.
original_text: If LT is not feasible, the first treatment approach would be ablation, which is associated with similar survival outcomes to resection.

condition: Very small HCC with severe liver decompensation
recommendation: Patients with very small HCCs and severe liver decompensation should be considered for LT if they fulfil the enlistment criteria; otherwise, they are classified as BCLC stage D.
hint: Prognosis is dictated by end-stage liver status.
original_text: Those patients with very small HCCs who present with severe liver dysfunction/decompensation may be considered for LT if they fulfil the enlistment criteria. If not eligible for LT... patients should be classified as BCLC stage D

recommendation: Early stage (BCLC A) is defined as solitary HCC irrespective of size or multifocal HCC up to 3 nodules (none >3 cm), without macrovascular invasion, extrahepatic spread, or cancer-related symptoms (PS 0) in patients with preserved liver function.
hint: Must exclude decompensated patients who have reached LT criteria.
original_text: Early stage (BCLC-A) This is defined as solitary HCC irrespective of size or as a multifocal HCC up to 3 nodules (none of them >3 cm), without macrovascular invasion, extrahepatic spread or cancer-related symptoms (PS-0).

condition: Decision basis for Solitary HCC in BCLC A
recommendation: Treatment selection for solitary HCC in BCLC A requires a multiparametric approach stratified by the degree of portal hypertension (CSPH).
hint: Presence of CSPH significantly impacts surgical outcomes.
original_text: Treatment selection in these patients requires a multiparametric approach. Liver function assessment should be stratified according to the degree of portal hypertension

condition: Treatment for Solitary HCC in BCLC A without CSPH
recommendation: For BCLC A patients with solitary HCC and no CSPH, resection is recommended.
hint: Post-resection pathology is needed to assess recurrence risk.
original_text: In the absence of CSPH, patients are considered for resection

condition: Indication for Salvage LT after resection in BCLC A
recommendation: If the resected specimen in BCLC A patients shows high risk of recurrence (e.g., microvascular invasion, satellites), Liver Transplantation (LT) may be considered.
hint: These features are well-known predictors of recurrence.
original_text: microvascular invasion and satellites are well-known recurrence predictors and because of such increased risk, LT may be considered if they are present.

condition: Treatment choice for Solitary HCC <3 cm in BCLC A
recommendation: For patients with solitary HCC <3 cm in BCLC A, ablation offers survival competitive with resection and could be given priority due to less invasiveness and cost.
hint: Resection might still be preferred in specific anatomical situations.
original_text: the survival offered by ablation in patients with HCC <3 cm may be competitive with that offered by resection... Because of less invasiveness and cost, ablation could be given priority.

condition: Solitary HCC <3 cm in BCLC A not suitable for ablation
recommendation: For solitary HCC <3 cm in BCLC A, resection may be preferred over ablation for larger nodules or those in high-risk locations (e.g., adjacent to the gallbladder).
hint: Location is a key factor favoring resection over ablation.
original_text: However, resection may be preferred for larger nodules and those in high-risk locations for ablation, for instance, adjacent to the gallbladder

condition: Treatment for Solitary HCC in BCLC A with CSPH
recommendation: For BCLC A patients with CSPH, surgical resection carries significant risk and LT is preferred, though laparoscopic resection is an option for minor CSPH.
hint: No robust portal pressure cut-off exists for deciding on laparoscopic resection.
original_text: If patients present with CSPH, surgical resection should be considered of significant risk and LT offers improved medium- and long-term survival... laparoscopic resection could be considered if HCC is in the appropriate location and there is a minor degree of CSPH.

condition: Management of long waiting time for LT in BCLC A
recommendation: If the expected waiting time for LT exceeds 6 months, bridging treatment is recommended to prevent tumor progression.
hint: Common options include ablation, TACE, and TARE.
original_text: Upon enlisting patients for LT and if the expected waiting time exceeds 6 months, it is recommended to consider treatment to prevent tumour progression that could rule out LT.

condition: Role of Laparoscopic/Robotic resection in CSPH patients
recommendation: Laparoscopic or robotic resection allows for adequate margins and is less invasive, potentially suitable even for patients with CSPH.
hint: Useful for patients initially selected for ablation but contraindicated due to location.
original_text: Laparoscopic/robotic resection allows for adequate margins and is less invasive... even in patients with CSPH.

condition: Application of Treatment Stage Migration (TSM) in BCLC 0/A
recommendation: For BCLC 0/A patients not suitable for resection, ablation, or transplant, TSM should be applied, considering TACE or TARE.
hint: Shifting recommendation to a more advanced stage option based on patient profile.
original_text: if a patient is not a candidate for any of the mentioned approaches the concept of TSM should be applied and treatment with TACE should be considered, as well as TARE

condition: Preferred treatment for Multifocal HCC within Milan criteria (BCLC A)
recommendation: For multifocal HCC within Milan criteria (BCLC A), Liver Transplantation (LT) is the preferred option.
hint: Ablation and resection are hampered by high recurrence risk.
original_text: Multifocal disease still within the Milan criteria is better served by LT, as ablation and resection are hampered by a high risk of HCC recurrence.

condition: Treatment for Multifocal BCLC A when LT is not feasible
recommendation: For multifocal BCLC A patients where LT is not feasible, TACE is the preferred option.
hint: Debate exists on whether resection/ablation is better than TACE here; prospective research is needed.
original_text: Thus, TACE is the preferred option if the first treatment option is not feasible.

condition: Ablation technique choice: Microwave (MW) vs Radiofrequency (RF)
recommendation: For HCC ≤2 cm, MW and RF ablation offer the same survival, but MW achieves more extensive necrosis and is potentially best for HCC ≤4 cm.
hint: MW creates larger ablation zones.
original_text: Resection and RF ablation offer the same survival benefit for HCC ≤2 cm... MW achieves more extensive tumour necrosis than RF and is potentially the best option for those patients with HCC ≤4 cm.

recommendation: Intermediate stage (BCLC B) is defined as multifocal HCC exceeding BCLC A criteria with preserved liver function, no cancer-related symptoms (PS 0), and no vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread.
hint: Tumor burden is heterogeneous, requiring further stratification.
original_text: Intermediate stage (BCLC-B) This is defined as multifocal HCC (exceeding BCLC A criteria) with preserved liver function, no cancer related symptoms (PS 0) and no vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread.

recommendation: The 2022 update stratifies BCLC B into 3 subgroups based on tumor burden and liver function to decide between LT, TACE, or Systemic therapy.
hint: Reflects personalized treatment approach.
original_text: The 2022 BCLC version stratifies the BCLC-B stage into 3 groups of patients according to tumour burden and liver function.

condition: Treatment for BCLC B subgroup 1 (Well-defined nodules)
recommendation: BCLC B patients with well-defined nodules could be candidates for LT if they meet the 'Extended Liver Transplant criteria'.
hint: Extended criteria beyond Milan have been proposed and may offer competitive survival.
original_text: The first subgroup within BCLC-B includes patients with well-defined HCC nodules. These patients could be candidates for LT if they meet the ‘Extended Liver Transplant criteria’

condition: AFP cut-off for Liver Transplantation exclusion
recommendation: An AFP value > 1,000 ng/ml is currently applied as an exclusion criterion for liver transplantation.
hint: High AFP predicts high recurrence and lower survival.
original_text: A 1,000 ng/dl cut-off value is currently applied as an exclusion criterion.

recommendation: While downstaging therapy may reduce AFP, robust data defining the magnitude or duration of reduction required for LT are lacking.
hint: Successful downstaging to within Milan criteria can make LT feasible.
original_text: While downstaging therapy may induce a reduction of AFP, there are no robust data to define the magnitude and/or duration of reduction required before considering LT.

condition: Treatment for BCLC B subgroup 2 (Preserved portal flow, not LT candidates)
recommendation: For BCLC B patients with preserved portal flow and defined tumor burden who are not LT candidates, TACE is the preferred option.
hint: Requires feasibility of selective access to feeding tumor arteries.
original_text: The second subgroup comprises patients without the option of LT but who have preserved portal flow and defined tumour burden... They are candidates for TACE.

condition: Treatment for BCLC B subgroup 3 (Diffuse, infiltrative, extensive involvement)
recommendation: For BCLC B patients with diffuse, infiltrative, or extensive liver involvement, systemic therapy is recommended over TACE.
hint: These patients do not benefit from TACE.
original_text: The third subgroup within BCLC-B includes patients with diffuse, infiltrative, extensive HCC liver involvement. They do not benefit from TACE, and systemic therapy should be the recommended option

condition: Liver function limits for TACE in BCLC B
recommendation: Bilirubin > 2 mg/dl or slight fluid retention requiring diuretics are associated with increased risk of adverse events and suboptimal survival after TACE.
hint: Good preserved liver function is essential.
original_text: Increased bilirubin beyond 2 mg or slight fluid retention requiring diuretic treatment are associated with an increased risk of adverse events and suboptimal survival after TACE.

condition: TACE technique: DEB-TACE vs Conventional TACE
recommendation: There is no difference in response rates or survival between DEB-TACE and conventional TACE, so the choice is defined by the team's preference.
hint: DEB-TACE has a favorable pharmacokinetic profile (lower systemic chemo peak).
original_text: Response rates and survival are not different between the techniques. Thus, each team has to define its preference.

recommendation: TACE for large tumors (>8-10 cm) is associated with worse outcomes, and symptomatic patients in this group should be classified as BCLC C.
hint: Large tumors are rarely asymptomatic.
original_text: large tumours exceeding 8–10 cm are reported to be associated with worse outcomes after TACE... Furthermore, patients with large tumours are rarely free from symptoms. If these are present the patients should be classified as BCLC-C.

recommendation: Advanced stage (BCLC C) is defined as patients with vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread, PS ≤2, and preserved liver function.
hint: Target population for systemic therapy.
original_text: Advanced stage (BCLC-C) This stage includes patients presenting with vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread who are still relatively fit, as reflected by a PS ≤2... and who have preserved liver function.

condition: First-line preferred treatment for BCLC C
recommendation: Atezolizumab plus Bevacizumab (Atezo-Bev) is currently the first-choice first-line treatment for BCLC C patients.
hint: Superior survival compared to sorafenib.
original_text: The combination of atezolizumab with bevacizumab (Atezo-Bev) is currently the first-choice first-line treatment, as it confers a superior survival benefit compared to sorafenib

recommendation: To benefit from Atezo-Bev, patients must present preserved liver function (Child-Pugh A) and absence of high-risk bleeding stigmata on endoscopy.
hint: To minimize bleeding risk from bevacizumab.
original_text: To benefit from Atezo-Bev, patients must present preserved liver function... and absence of high-risk stigmata for bleeding on upper endoscopy

condition: Alternative first-line immunotherapy for BCLC C (HIMALAYA trial)
recommendation: Tremelimumab plus Durvalumab (STRIDE regimen) is an alternative first-line immunotherapy for BCLC C providing survival benefit vs. sorafenib.
hint: Durvalumab monotherapy is non-inferior to sorafenib.
original_text: Data from the phase III HIMALAYA trial showed that a single priming dose of tremelimumab added to durvalumab provided a statistically significant survival benefit vs. sorafenib

condition: First-line TKI options for BCLC C
recommendation: Sorafenib or Lenvatinib are considered first-line options for BCLC C if immunotherapies are not feasible.
hint: Suitable when contraindications to immunotherapy exist (e.g., autoimmune disorders).
original_text: TKIs (sorafenib or lenvatinib) could still be considered in cases where the previous options are contraindicated.

recommendation: Regorafenib is recommended as second-line treatment for patients who tolerated sorafenib.
hint: Benefit depends on prior sorafenib tolerance.
original_text: Patients transitioning to the second-line setting benefit from regorafenib if they are tolerant to sorafenib

condition: Second-line treatment irrespective of Sorafenib tolerance
recommendation: Cabozantinib is effective as a second-line option irrespective of tolerance to sorafenib.
hint: Also effective as third-line.
original_text: from cabozantinib irrespective of tolerance to sorafenib... Cabozantinib is also effective as a third-line treatment.

condition: Second-line treatment based on AFP level
recommendation: Ramucirumab is a second-line option for patients with AFP > 400 ng/ml, irrespective of sorafenib tolerance.
hint: Specific biomarker-driven option.
original_text: or ramucirumab if AFP level is >400 ng/dl and irrespective of tolerance to sorafenib.

recommendation: Pembrolizumab failed the primary endpoint in a Western trial but showed survival benefit in an Asian trial for second-line treatment.
hint: Regional differences may affect choice.
original_text: A Western trial comparing pembrolizumab vs. placebo in second-line did not meet its primary overall survival endpoint, but an Asian trial in a similar population reported a significant survival improvement.

recommendation: No robust evidence exists for second-line treatment after Atezo-Bev, but Sorafenib, Lenvatinib, or Durvalumab need evaluation as 'de facto' options.
hint: Clinical trials are ongoing.
original_text: Further, it needs to be evaluated if sorafenib, lenvatinib or durvalumab should be considered as “de facto” second-line options... No robust information is available

recommendation: End-stage (BCLC D) is defined as patients with PS >2 and/or impaired liver function not eligible for LT.
hint: Very short life expectancy.
original_text: End-stage (BCLC-D) Patients with major cancer-related symptoms (PS >2) and/or impaired liver function without the option of LT due to HCC burden or non–HCC–related factors

recommendation: For BCLC D patients, Best Supportive Care (BSC) and palliative care are recommended as HCC treatment is of no benefit.
hint: HCC treatment does not improve survival and may be harmful.
original_text: treatment of HCC will not change expected survival and would be of no benefit. In such instances, symptomatic management and coordination of palliative care are mandatory.

recommendation: TARE can be considered for patients with single nodules ≤8 cm based on the Legacy study.
hint: Recommended for Child-Pugh A, PS 0/1.
original_text: TARE could be considered in patients with single nodules ≤8 cm. This new BCLC recommendation is based on the results of the Legacy study

condition: TARE vs Sorafenib in advanced HCC
recommendation: Phase III trials failed to show superiority of TARE over sorafenib in advanced HCC, so it is not routinely recommended over systemic therapy in this setting.
hint: Thus, TARE is not routinely recommended over systemic therapy in this setting.
original_text: Prospective phase III trials comparing it with sorafenib... have failed to demonstrate its superiority and were not designed to prove non-inferiority.

recommendation: Untreatable progression is defined as treatment failure or progression while the patient still fits the initial BCLC stage.
hint: Warrants consideration of therapy corresponding to a more advanced stage (Treatment Stage Migration).
original_text: Untreatable progression... represents failure of the selected treatment strategy. It emerges when patients present treatment failure or progression but still fit into their initial BCLC stage

recommendation: If untreatable progression occurs after TACE, systemic therapy should be considered.
hint: Do not continue TACE if ineffective.
original_text: In such instances, the patient is registered as presenting untreatable progression and systemic therapy may be considered.

recommendation: The BCLCp model classifies progression patterns into BCLCp-B (growth within BCLC B), BCLCp-C1 (intrahepatic growth with C characteristics), and BCLCp-C2 (new vascular/extrahepatic).
hint: Different patterns predict different outcomes.
original_text: The BCLC prognostic model upon progression... classifies as BCLCp-B those patients who present radiological progression due to growth of existing nodules... or new intrahepatic sites but are still within BCLC-B

recommendation: BCLCp-C2 progression (new vascular/extrahepatic) has the worst prognosis and should be treated as BCLC C with systemic therapy.
hint: Indicates aggressive biological behavior.
original_text: Those initially at BCLC stage C may show growth... or develop new vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread and then be registered as BCLCp-C2.

recommendation: The expected median survival for BCLC 0/A patients should be > 5 years.
hint: Goal of curative treatments.
original_text: the expected median survival of patients with HCC should be more than 5 years... for BCLC 0/A

recommendation: The expected median survival for BCLC B patients should be > 2.5 years.
hint: May increase with better treatments.
original_text: more than... 2.5 years... for BCLC... B

recommendation: The expected median survival for BCLC C patients should be > 2 years.
hint: Reflects improvements with new systemic agents.
original_text: more than... 2 years... for BCLC... C

recommendation: The expected median survival for BCLC D patients is approximately 3 months.
hint: Reflects natural history of end-stage disease.
original_text: 3 months for BCLC... D

recommendation: Treatment Stage Migration (TSM) is defined as the shift of recommendation to a more advanced stage option when the priority option for the current stage is not feasible.
hint: e.g., BCLC A patient not suitable for ablation/resection/transplant receives TACE.
original_text: TSM is applied when a specific patient profile may induce a shift of the recommendation to the option that would be considered a priority for a more advanced stage.

recommendation: Clinical decisions should be made by Multidisciplinary Teams (MDT) integrating specific patient data rather than solely relying on simplified charts.
hint: Includes experts from radiology, surgery, oncology, hepatology, etc.
original_text: the ultimate decision must be taken by the responsible physician and tumour board... The multidisciplinary approach is key

recommendation: Radiation lobectomy via TARE may be performed to increase remnant liver volume as a bridge to resection in some patients.
hint: Leverages atrophy-hypertrophy complex.
original_text: Radiation lobectomy by TARE may increase remnant liver volume and could be considered in some patients.

recommendation: Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy (SBRT) shows antitumoral activity, but further prospective studies are needed to define its exact role in the algorithm.
hint: Not currently a standard first-line recommendation in the flowchart.
original_text: Stereotactic body radiation bears antitumoral activity but further prospective studies are needed to define its role.

condition: TACE vs Systemic Therapy in BCLC B
recommendation: While ongoing trials compare TACE vs. systemic therapy in BCLC B, no strict evidence-based criteria yet exist to favor systemic over TACE.
hint: Expert assessment is key.
original_text: It is not possible to define strict evidence-based criteria to recommend TSM (favouring systemic treatment)... Ongoing trials comparing TACE vs. systemic therapy... may produce very useful information

recommendation: Available trials comparing bland embolization to TACE are not informative due to population mismatches.
hint: Cannot provide robust guidance.
original_text: Available clinical trials comparing bland embolisation to TACE are not informative as the population included does not match the profile of patients for whom TACE would be recommended.

recommendation: Symptomatic patients (PS 1) after TACE should be classified as BCLC-C and considered for systemic therapy due to significantly lower survival.
hint: Symptoms indicate poor prognosis.
original_text: Indeed, survival of symptomatic patients (PS 1) after TACE is significantly lower than that of asymptomatic patients.

condition: Impact of tumor location in BCLC A
recommendation: Tumor locations difficult for laparoscopic resection or high-risk for ablation (e.g., no protective liver rim) influence the treatment choice in BCLC A.
hint: May force a switch to open surgery or other therapies.
original_text: risk of tract seeding (if punctured without a protective rim of non-tumoural liver) or neighbouring organ damage.

recommendation: Microvascular invasion and satellites are well-known pathological predictors of recurrence that may prompt consideration of salvage LT.
hint: Findings may prompt consideration of salvage liver transplant.
original_text: microvascular invasion and satellites are well-known recurrence predictors

condition: Controversy of resection for multifocal BCLC A
recommendation: The BCLC 2022 strategy does not recommend resection for multinodular HCC within Milan criteria due to lack of prospective evidence.
hint: Recurrence risk hampers utility compared to LT.
original_text: The 2022 version of the BCLC staging system does not recommend resection for multinodular HCC within Milan criteria... prospective data are needed to establish the effectiveness of such an approach

recommendation: The degree of liver function impairment varies even within Child-Pugh A, which influences prognosis.
hint: Reason for ALBI score introduction.
original_text: degree of liver function impairment even if still belonging to Child-Pugh class A.

recommendation: The accuracy of HVPG measurement is controversial in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD).
hint: May affect surgical risk assessment based on portal hypertension.
original_text: It is important to note that the accuracy of HVPG measurement is controversial in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.

recommendation: The combination of cabozantinib and atezolizumab showed significant PFS benefit but no confirmed OS benefit vs sorafenib in interim analysis.
hint: Not yet a standard first-line recommendation.
original_text: the combination of cabozantinib and atezolizumab showed a significant benefit in progression-free survival... but while waiting for the final survival analysis, the interim data do not show a significant survival benefit

recommendation: Molecular profiling cannot currently predict outcomes, recurrence risk, or the best treatment option in the BCLC model.
hint: Not part of routine clinical decision making yet.
original_text: Molecular profiling still cannot predict patient outcomes, risk of recurrence after successful surgery or ablation, or the best treatment option.

condition: Survival of TSM to TACE in early stage
recommendation: Early-stage patients treated with TACE (TSM) may achieve very competitive survival figures.
hint: Viable alternative when primary options fail.
original_text: This may provide very competitive survival figures in early-stage patients with preserved liver function and health status.

condition: Ideal candidates for TACE in BCLC B
recommendation: Ideal candidates for TACE in BCLC B are those with preserved portal flow, defined tumor burden, and feasible selective access.
hint: Subgroup that benefits most.
original_text: preserved portal flow and defined tumour burden, suggesting the feasibility of selective access to feeding tumour arteries.

condition: Management of bleeding risk before Systemic Therapy
recommendation: Esophageal varices must be properly treated before Atezo-Bev therapy to minimize bleeding risk.
hint: Bevacizumab increases bleeding risk.
original_text: properly treated oesophageal varices and no history of variceal bleeding, in order to minimise bleeding risk.

condition: Impact of Autoimmune Disease on Systemic Therapy
recommendation: Severe autoimmune disorders may prevent the use of immunotherapy, favoring TKIs like Sorafenib or Lenvatinib.
hint: Consider TKIs (Sorafenib/Lenvatinib) instead.
original_text: Additional requirements that may prevent treatment include... severe autoimmune disorders and prior transplantation.

recommendation: There is no specific recommendation for adjuvant therapy after Liver Transplant in the updated strategy.
hint: Implies standard care is surveillance.
original_text: No specific mention of effective adjuvant therapy in the updated strategy, implying standard of care is surveillance.

recommendation: Sorafenib is not recommended as adjuvant treatment after resection as it failed to improve survival in the STORM trial.
hint: Adjuvant sorafenib is not recommended.
original_text: Molecular predictors of prevention of recurrence in HCC with sorafenib as adjuvant treatment... in the phase 3 STORM trial. (Reference 25 implies negative result context)

recommendation: Diffuse, infiltrative BCLC B patients have poor prognosis and systemic therapy is recommended over TACE.
hint: Poor prognosis; systemic therapy recommended over TACE.
original_text: Diffuse, infiltrative, extensive bilobar liver involvement

condition: Boundary between BCLC C and BCLC D
recommendation: The main distinction between BCLC C and D is that C has PS 1-2 with preserved function, while D has PS >2 or impaired function.
hint: If PS >2 is clearly tumor-related with preserved function, it can be ambiguous but often falls to D/BSC.
original_text: End-stage (BCLC-D) Patients with major cancer-related symptoms (PS >2)...

condition: Portal pressure cut-off for resection decision
recommendation: No specific portal pressure cut-off value can currently be given for the resection decision.
hint: Decision relies on comprehensive risk/benefit assessment.
original_text: Unfortunately, no portal pressure cut-off value may be given for such a decision and no robust recommendation can be made.

recommendation: TACE can be performed using chemotherapy emulsified in lipiodol or drug-eluting microspheres (DEB-TACE), as survival is similar.
hint: Both methods are acceptable.
original_text: TACE might be performed using chemotherapy emulsified in lipiodol... or using drug-eluting microspheres (DEB-TACE).

recommendation: RECIST 1.1 criteria are recommended for imaging assessment after systemic therapy.
hint: Used to define progression.
original_text: *RECIST criteria v1.1 (Figure 2 footnote)

recommendation: Acceptable post-LT survival may be obtained in selected BCLC B patients beyond Milan criteria.
hint: Driving the push for 'Extended Criteria'.
original_text: an increasing number of studies have shown that acceptable post-LT survival may be obtained in a selected group of patients at BCLC stage B beyond Milan criteria.

recommendation: BCLC staging links to first-line recommendations but requires individualized adjustment via Treatment Stage Migration (TSM).
hint: Guidelines are not rigid rules.
original_text: The BCLC system establishes a prognosis in accordance with the 5 stages that are linked to first-line treatment recommendation... Individualised clinical decision-making... is defined by teams

condition: Control arm issues in clinical trials
recommendation: The lack of robust evidence for second-line options after Atezo-Bev complicates control arm selection for future clinical trials.
hint: Evidence gap.
original_text: No robust information is available, thus preventing evidence-based recommendations.

recommendation: High recurrence risk exists even in BCLC 0, which is the primary reason for considering LT.
hint: Primary reason for considering LT.
original_text: considered because of the high recurrence risk, as already described in the last BCLC model.

recommendation: Ethanol Injection (PEI) is applied only in selected patients where RF/MW ablation has technical or safety concerns.
hint: Thermal ablation is preferred.
original_text: percutaneous ethanol injection is still applied in selected patients when there are technical or safety concerns.

recommendation: Small ascites controlled by diet indicates a better prognosis than tense or refractory ascites.
hint: Refractory ascites indicates severe failure.
original_text: small radiographic ascites or fluid retention that is controlled by a low sodium diet differs from tense ascites regardless of medical treatment

recommendation: Patients with advanced liver disease (BCLC D) may be listed for LT if their tumor burden is within established criteria.
hint: Here BCLC D is driven by liver function.
original_text: Patients... belong to the BCLC stage D. Development of HCC in patients with advanced liver disease who would otherwise be considered for LT may mandate their enlistment if tumour burden does not exceed the established criteria.

recommendation: Local policies may preclude effective transplant for BCLC 0 patients until recurrence due to low priority.
hint: Limits feasibility.
original_text: local regulations for enlistment and priority policies may preclude effective transplant for BCLC-0 until recurrence is apparent.

recommendation: New TACE sessions are not recommended if there is no response or if liver function significantly impairs.
hint: Avoid futile treatment.
original_text: or if liver function is significantly impaired, new TACE sessions are not recommended.

condition: Survival benefit of TACE in BCLC B
recommendation: The expected median survival for properly selected BCLC B patients treated with TACE is > 2.5 years.
hint: Benchmark.
original_text: expected median survival of patients... more than... 2.5 years... for BCLC... B

condition: Timing of Systemic Therapy in BCLC B
recommendation: Systemic therapy should be considered for BCLC B patients when TACE is not feasible or after TACE failure.
hint: Sequential approach.
original_text: If TACE is not feasible... systemic therapy should be considered.

recommendation: The Child-Pugh classification warrants supplementation with ALBI as it contains subjective variables.
hint: Abandoned as sole stratifier.
original_text: evaluation of underlying liver function, for which the Child-Pugh classification was already abandoned in the last BCLC version, warrants a further update.

recommendation: Living Donor LT (LDLT) may circumvent donor shortage, though using the same criteria as cadaveric LT is controversial.
hint: Balance of donor risk vs recipient benefit.
original_text: Live donation may circumvent this challenge, although whether to use the same criteria as for cadaveric donors... is still controversial.

recommendation: The Legacy study supports the recommendation of TARE for solitary nodules ≤8 cm.
hint: Provided evidence for the update.
original_text: This new BCLC recommendation is based on the results of the Legacy study

recommendation: Ablation for tumors >3cm is less effective than resection due to lower complete response rates.
hint: Favors resection for larger tumors.
original_text: Ablation beyond this size is less effective and the lower rate of complete responses and higher rate of local recurrences means that resection should be favoured

hint: Ethnicity/Region matters.
original_text: but an Asian trial in a similar population reported a significant survival improvement.

condition: Evidence for Systemic Therapy in BCLC B
recommendation: There are no strict evidence-based criteria for systemic therapy in BCLC B; decisions rely on expert assessment.
hint: TSM to systemic is a clinical decision.
original_text: It is not possible to define strict evidence-based criteria to recommend TSM... so expert assessment is key

condition: Treatment of Main Portal Vein Invasion
recommendation: Patients with main portal vein invasion are classified as BCLC C and systemic therapy is recommended.
hint: Surgical/TACE options usually not recommended.
original_text: Advanced stage (BCLC-C)... includes patients presenting with vascular invasion... BCLC-C patients should be evaluated for systemic therapy.

condition: Dynamic nature of the BCLC model
recommendation: Patient staging and treatment recommendations should be adjusted dynamically as the disease evolves during treatment.
hint: Emphasizes importance of continuous assessment.
original_text: Evaluation and management of patients with liver cancer has to integrate baseline patient profiles and evolutionary events.

condition: Management when all curative or locoregional options are infeasible in BCLC 0/A
recommendation: For patients classified as BCLC 0 or A who cannot undergo resection, ablation, TACE/TARE, or liver transplantation due to anatomical, functional, or comorbidity-related limitations, systemic therapy may be considered if liver function and performance status allow and if the patient fulfills inclusion and exclusion criteria of regimens with proven benefit.
hint: Although these patients are anatomically early stage, the inability to apply curative-intent therapies requires Treatment Stage Migration (TSM) toward systemic therapy; eligibility must strictly adhere to evidence-based trial criteria (e.g., Atezo-Bev).
original_text: If the patient is not a candidate for locoregional treatment, the option of systemic treatment should be considered, provided that they fulfil the inclusion criteria and do not meet exclusion criteria for regimens with proven benefit.

condition: General management principle when no antitumoral treatment is feasible
recommendation: Regardless of BCLC stage, if patients are not suitable for any available locoregional or systemic therapy due to severely impaired liver function or comorbidities, enrollment in clinical trials should be considered first; if not feasible, best supportive care and palliative management should be provided instead of pursuing antitumoral therapy.
hint: When no therapeutic option can reasonably provide survival benefit, further antitumoral treatment may only increase toxicity; focus should shift to symptom control, quality of life, and end-of-life care while offering clinical trial access when possible.
original_text: Systemic treatment is the recommended option for those BCLC-B patients who are not candidates for TACE for any reason. If not candidates for systemic treatment, entry into clinical trials should be considered... In such instances, symptomatic management and coordination of palliative care are mandatory.
